# Reference: Privacy & Data Handling at the Individual Tier

Default behavior on training, retention, telemetry, opt-out paths. See [`citations.md`](../citations.md) for sources.

This is the dimension where 2025-2026 saw the most consequential policy shifts, all in the same direction: **the "default" for individual paid tiers shifted from "we don't train on you" toward "we do train on you unless you opt out."**

## Specific policy details

### Anthropic / Claude Code [3][4][5]

- **August 28, 2025:** Anthropic updates consumer terms.
- **October 8, 2025:** existing-user selection deadline.
- **What changed:** consumer plans (Free, Pro, Max) ask users to choose whether their conversations and coding sessions can be used for model training. The choice is presented; the **TechCrunch coverage of the policy change** characterized this as a "default opt-in" framing for new accounts, while the Anthropic page wording emphasizes "giving users the choice" — see Gaps below.
- **Retention if opted in:** "in a de-identified format for up to 5 years in our model training pipelines" [4].
- **Retention if opted out:** 30 days for new chats; ongoing chats may be retained for safety review [4].
- **Excluded:** "commercial services: Claude for Work, Government, Education, and API access through Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Vertex AI" — no training use, ZDR available [3].
- **Trust & safety violations:** inputs/outputs 2 years; classification scores 7 years [4].

### GitHub Copilot [14]

- **Effective April 24, 2026.**
- **Affected:** Free, Pro, Pro+.
- **Excluded:** Business, Enterprise.
- **Data collected by default:** "inputs, outputs, code snippets, and associated context" — encompasses accepted/modified suggestions, surrounding context, comments, file names, feature interaction patterns, feedback ratings.
- **Opt-out:** Settings → Copilot → Features → "Allow GitHub to use my data for AI model training."
- **Previous opt-out preserved.**
- **Important caveat:** "Copilot processes private repository code during active use." Source code at rest is not used for training (unchanged from prior policy).

### Cursor [9]

- **Privacy Mode ON (manual):** "None of your code will ever be trained on by us or any third-party." ZDR with all model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Fireworks).
- **Privacy Mode OFF:** Cursor collects "codebase data, prompts, editor actions, code snippets" used to train models. Inference providers (Baseten, Together AI, Fireworks) temporarily access data.
- **Embeddings persistence:** Even with Privacy Mode ON, embeddings and metadata (file hashes, names) "may persist in Cursor's database."
- **Account vintage:** Accounts created before October 15, 2025 have different sharing restrictions with model providers.
- **Per-plan defaults:** the public docs page surfaced in this run does NOT specify defaults per plan; Discovery agent reported Free/Pro = OFF by default, Business/Teams = ON by default.

### Gemini Code Assist Individuals [20]

- Free tier: code prompts/answers may be collected and used for model training; opt-out in settings.
- Data disconnected from Google Account before human review; retained up to 18 months disconnected.
- Standard / Enterprise editions: prompts NOT collected, NOT used for training.

### Antigravity [agent research]

- Official position: code not stored permanently for training without opt-in.
- Opt-out toggle in Settings (users report difficulty locating it in forum threads).
- SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant claimed.
- Paid AI Pro / Ultra subscribers reported to have stronger data protections per developer forum threads.
- Sandboxed agent execution: agents cannot access host system outside workspace without permission.

### Windsurf [agent research, ToS-individual]

- **Autocomplete (Tab) content:** may be used to train discriminative (ranking) models — not generative; opt-out keeps data sent to servers but not retained for training.
- **Chat (Cascade) content:** may be used to train both generative and discriminative models; content anonymized before training.
- **Hard opt-out:** opting out of chat training disables Chat Services entirely.
- **Zero-Data Retention (ZDR):** individual users can opt-in from profile page.
- **Compliance:** SOC 2 Type II; Enterprise adds HIPAA, FedRAMP/DoD, ITAR, RBAC, SCIM.

### IBM Bob [agent research from official docs]

- Telemetry is opt-in (not collected by default per `bob.ibm.com/docs/shell/configuration/telemetry-data-shell` per Discovery agent extraction).
- Session data removed from IBM Cloud after session ends per IBM statement.
- Prompt sanitization to block PII and injection.
- Customer-cloud deployment available for data-residency.
- **Explicit "code not used for training" pledge: NOT surfaced in fetched docs.** This is a real gap in the privacy story for Bob.

## Cross-platform observations

1. **Three of the six platforms (Claude Code [3], GitHub Copilot [14], Gemini Code Assist Individual [20]) now use individual-tier code/prompts for training by default.** All three offer opt-out. None makes opt-out one-click prominent in their primary UI.

2. **The line between "consumer/individual" and "commercial/enterprise" privacy is now the most material privacy line.** All three platforms above maintain "no training" guarantees only for Business/Enterprise/API/commercial tiers. A small team using individual subscriptions to keep costs down is materially less private than the same team on a Business plan, even if they opt out (because data may still flow temporarily for inference / processing).

3. **Cursor's Privacy Mode is a true ZDR mode** [9] — when on, code is not used for training and ZDR is enforced with model providers. But the user must opt in, and embeddings/metadata may still persist.

4. **Windsurf's hard opt-out** [agent research] is more punitive than competitors' — opting out of chat data sharing disables chat entirely. Privacy-conscious individual users who want chat have no middle ground other than ZDR.

5. **IBM Bob has the strongest data-residency story** (customer-cloud deployment) but the weakest "code not for training" surface evidence in fetched material. Buyers should request this in writing.

## Gaps and limitations

- The Anthropic consumer terms update [3] is described as offering "the choice" — the TechCrunch summary (referenced via Discovery agent) characterized the new behavior as opt-in to training by default for new accounts. The two characterizations are not strictly contradictory but suggest a default-shift framing the Anthropic page itself does not state directly. The verified Anthropic news page [3] gives the user the choice; the framing of "default" may differ between commercial accounts and consumer accounts. Buyers should treat training default as opt-in to data use unless they confirm otherwise.
- Per-plan Privacy Mode defaults for Cursor are not stated on the public Data Use page [9]; the agent's claim of OFF-by-default for Pro is not directly verified in fetched docs.
- Antigravity's opt-out user-experience problems are documented in developer forum threads but not in this run's direct fetches.
- Bob's "code not used for training" pledge is absent from fetched material; this gap is itself a meaningful finding.
